passage_text: Researchers conducted a randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of a novel antihypertensive agent, Hypto‑X, in adults with stage‑1 hypertension. Two hundred participants were enrolled and randomly assigned to either Hypto‑X (n=100) or placebo (n=100). Baseline systolic blood pressure (SBP) was measured after a 5‑minute seated rest and averaged over three readings. After 4 weeks of daily dosing, SBP was reassessed using the same protocol. The study aimed to determine the mean change in SBP and assess safety profiles. The investigators also collected data on adverse events, heart rate, and renal function. The primary outcome was the mean difference in SBP between groups at week 4. Secondary outcomes included the proportion of participants achieving target SBP <130 mmHg and incidence of treatment‑related adverse events. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04567890).
stem: Based on the data presented in the table, which statement best describes the observed effect of Hypto‑X on systolic blood pressure after 4 weeks?

options.A: Hypto‑X increased systolic blood pressure compared to placebo.
options.B: Hypto‑X had no statistically significant effect on systolic blood pressure.
options.C: Hypto‑X reduced systolic blood pressure by approximately 13 mmHg more than placebo.
options.D: Hypto‑X reduced systolic blood pressure by approximately 6 mmHg more than placebo.

explanation: Hypto-X change = 138.5 - 122.3 = 16.2 mmHg; placebo change = 137.8 - 134.9 = 2.9 mmHg. The between-group difference in change is 13.3 mmHg (about 13 mmHg); the week-4 absolute difference is 12.6 mmHg.
trap: Option D (6 mmHg) matches neither the difference in change (13.3) nor the week-4 difference (12.6); using Hypto-X's raw change (16 mmHg) ignores the placebo response.

stem: Which design feature best ensures that baseline SBP is balanced between the Hypto-X and placebo groups?

options.A: Random assignment to Hypto-X or placebo

explanation: Correct: A) Random assignment balances baseline characteristics, such as SBP (138.5 versus 137.8 mmHg), between groups on average. Why the others are wrong: B) Blinding reduces observer and expectation bias but does not balance groups. C) Seated rest standardizes measurement conditions. D) Averaging readings improves measurement precision, not group balance.
trap: Choosing a measurement-standardization step (seated rest or averaged readings) as the way groups are balanced, when those steps only improve measurement quality.

stem: Calculate the percent reduction in systolic blood pressure for the Hypto‑X group from baseline to week 4.
explanation: Correct: B) (138.5 - 122.3)/138.5 x 100 = 11.7%. Why the others are wrong: A) 9.3% does not correspond to the correct baseline calculation. C) 13.2% divides the 16.2 mmHg drop by the week 4 value (122.3) instead of the baseline. D) 18.2% does not correspond to the correct calculation.
trap: Dividing the 16.2 mmHg drop by the week 4 value (16.2/122.3 = 13.2%) instead of the baseline, which gives option C.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?

options.A: Participants were randomly assigned to Hypto-X or placebo.
options.B: The primary outcome was the mean difference in SBP between groups at week 4.
options.C: Hypto-X lowered SBP in patients with chronic kidney disease.
options.D: Baseline SBP was measured after a 5-minute seated rest.

explanation: Correct: C) Renal function was collected, but the passage reports no results in patients with kidney disease, so the claim is unsupported. Why the others are wrong: A) Random assignment is stated. B) The primary outcome is stated as the mean difference in SBP at week 4. D) The seated-rest protocol is stated.
trap: Reading the mention of renal function monitoring as evidence of an effect in kidney disease, when the passage reports no such result.

stem: What is the approximate 95% CI for the difference in mean week 4 SBP between groups (Hypto-X minus placebo), using the SE of the difference?
explanation: Correct: A) Difference = 122.3 - 134.9 = -12.6 mmHg; SE = sqrt(8.7^2/100 + 9.1^2/100) = 1.26; 95% CI = -12.6 +/- 1.96 x 1.26, about -15.1 to -10.1. Why the others are wrong: B) -13.9 to -11.3 uses only 1 SE as the margin. C) -14.3 to -10.9 uses only the Hypto-X group's SE (0.87). D) -21.6 to -3.6 uses an SD (about 9) as the margin instead of an SE.
trap: Using an SD (about 9 mmHg) as the margin of error, or only one group's SE, instead of 1.96 x the SE of the difference.
